Once upon a time, in the days when the animals were just beginning, there lived a young leopard who was very proud of his spots. He admired them in every puddle. “Look,” he would say to the zebra, “no creature in all the world is half so handsome.” The zebra, who was wise, only flicked his tail. One morning, the leopard went to hunt and found that his spots, so splendid in the sunlight, were quite useless in the open grass, where every antelope could see him coming. He went home hungry that night — and the next — until he learned to wait in the shadows, where his spots became exactly what he needed.
